findings.evidence: “Over-pasting a report nobody acts on buries the signal as much as under-informing does.” This is generic communication advice; the adjacent outcome table already specifies what to show and when.
findings.fix: Keep the outcome table and the decision-versus-information cue. Record the redundant explanatory sentence as a removal.

findings.evidence: “needs review-and-fix” understates support for review-only requests, while “or passing document path(s)” suggests a path alone can trigger the skill. The description does not distinguish document review from PR review or plan execution.
findings.fix: Use when asked to review a design, spec, RFC, requirements document, or implementation plan for gaps, contradictions, or readiness—even if the user just wants a second opinion before building. Reviews named documents at their lifecycle stage in Superpowers, GSD, OpenSpec, Spec Kit, Kiro, BMAD, or a generic workflow. Reports findings and routes fixes through the appropriate framework only when authorized, then re-reviews up to the iteration cap. Supports independent reviewers via --cross-ai or the session model via --no-cross-ai. Not for drafting a new document, executing a plan, configuring reviewers, or reviewing a code diff or PR.

findings.evidence: The 560-line main file includes the full procedure for an “owner-started command, off unless [review] edit_lens_pass = true” that “the review loop never starts.” It also loads the lane-role and lens diagnostic tables for native-only reviews.
findings.fix: Keep the rule that the review loop never starts the edit-lens pass and the pre-spawn refusal stop condition in SKILL.md. Move the role, lens-note and diagnostic tables to a subprocess troubleshooting reference, and move the after-approval command, acceptance, rejection and recovery details to a reference loaded only when the owner requests that pass. Preserve all rules and examples in those destinations.

findings.evidence: “Remove $RUN_TMP_DIR (`rm -rf "$RUN_TMP_DIR"`) only when the Surface outcome is `Approved` and no lane is pending.” Cleanup is destructive, but the command does not verify that the path belongs to this run, especially after a resume pointer bypasses temp-directory creation.
findings.fix: Use a cleanup helper that verifies the resolved directory is a run directory under the expected temp root and matches this run's recorded identity before deleting it. On mismatch or missing proof, retain the directory and report its path. Keep the approval and no-pending gates.

findings.evidence: The first eval's setup only says to copy the scratch project and rename `aikit/`. Its roster names `fake/placeholder-model-1`, yet the eval expects a completed review and fixer dispatch without supplying a fake runtime, recording a reviewer response, or initializing git for the normal worktree branch.
findings.fix: Supply a repeatable setup that initializes a scratch git root, isolates the config, and uses a fake reviewer that advertises the fixture model and emits a known finding. Add an explicit review-only case that checks the finding is surfaced and no fixer or rewrite is dispatched without consent.

findings.evidence: “Draft a commit message for the config migration change I just staged” is an easy negative; the suite has 10 positives and 10 negatives, but several negatives are farther from the activation boundary than ordinary document tasks.
findings.fix: Replace two easy negatives with realistic queries that name the same artifacts but ask for a different action, such as copyediting a GSD PLAN.md without reviewing its substance or summarizing the decisions in an RFC without assessing it.

findings.evidence: “Pick the entry whose `archetype` equals the flagged archetype.” A fused Superpowers design exposes intent, requirements and design checklists, but the bundled profile assigns ownership to the design artifact and defines only a `design` route. A requirements finding in that file can therefore go to the generic fixer instead of brainstorming. The checklist's `Location: <section/lines>` format also does not guarantee an archetype tag.
findings.fix: Record the owning profile `doc_types` row for each input. For fused artifacts, use the row's owning archetype for rewrite routing unless the profile explicitly defines an override; use the fused list only to select review checklists. Include the document path in findings for multi-document runs, and surface any finding that cannot be bound to an input.

findings.evidence: “`probe-quota` probes each lane of the review order in order.” The implementation excludes native and skipped routes (`ai_kit_spec/routing.py:186`) and reuses fresh cached results (`ai_kit_spec/quota.py:290`). An unavailable lane can be skipped without being probed in this run.
findings.fix: Describe probing as refreshing only eligible entries whose cache rows are missing or stale, and describe reviewer selection as a separate ladder walk over those results and routing decisions. Report cached unavailability as cached, not as a fresh probe failure.

findings.evidence: The stage-gap template says “Reviewed <existing> as <archetype>,” but Step 0.6 says to stop before dispatch and offer that review. When only intent exists and the user asks for a plan review, the template falsely claims the intent was reviewed.
findings.fix: Use Step 0.6's offer in the Surface row: say no plan was reviewed, name the existing artifact and its stage, and offer to review it only if the user confirms.

findings.evidence: “`/gsd-review --phase <N>` writes it” is presented as universal. The upstream GSD command declares `gsd:review`, and its current plan workflow shows `/gsd:plan-phase <N> --reviews`; this reference does not tie the hyphenated spelling to an installed version or instruct the handoff to resolve it live.
findings.fix: Resolve both command spellings from the installed GSD command or backing skill before invoking or surfacing them. Cite the official GSD workflow and the date checked for the `REVIEWS.md` prerequisite; if the installed spelling cannot be confirmed, say so rather than emitting an exact command.

findings.evidence: “the harness's own 600000ms maximum” is stated as a fixed cap. Claude Code documents 600000 ms as a default configurable foreground ceiling, and other hosts have different limits.
findings.fix: Keep background execution as the default. Allow foreground execution only when the cumulative tiers fit the current host's verified timeout; if retaining the Claude Code number, label it a configurable default and cite the official environment-variable documentation with the date checked.
